'''Uri Banin''' ([[Hebrew language|Hebrew]]: אורי בנין) is an Israeli nanotechnologist and physical chemist and a professor at the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]], currently holding the Alfred & Erica Larisch Memorial Chair at the Institute of Chemistry. He is recognized as one of the pioneers of [[nanoscience]] in Israel.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://chemistry.huji.ac.il/people/uri-banin|title=Uri Banin|website=chemistry.huji.ac.il|access-date=2019-11-15}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=http://chem.ch.huji.ac.il/nano/ProfBanin.html|title=Prof. Uri Banin Research Group|website=chem.ch.huji.ac.il|access-date=2019-11-15}}</ref>

== Education ==
Following his military service, in 1986 Banin proceeded on to his academic career, receiving his [[Bachelor of Science]] degree in [[chemistry]] and [[physics]] from the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]] in 1989.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":3">{{Cite web|url=https://www.iit.it/scientific-technical-committee/83-uri-banin-cv-eng/file|title=PROFESSOR URI BANIN, CURRICULUM VITAE|last=|first=|date=|website=|access-date=2019-11-15|archive-date=2019-11-18|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191118111235/https://www.iit.it/scientific-technical-committee/83-uri-banin-cv-eng/file|url-status=dead}}</ref> He later received [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] from the Hebrew University, under the supervision of Sanford Ruhman in the field of [[Femtochemistry|femtosecond spectroscopy]],<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://chem.ch.huji.ac.il/sandy/Group/group.htm|title=Ruhman's Lab - The Group|website=chem.ch.huji.ac.il|access-date=2019-11-15|archive-date=2019-11-16|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191116011717/http://chem.ch.huji.ac.il/sandy/Group/group.htm|url-status=dead}}</ref> studying the [[Ultrashort pulse|ultrafast]] dynamics of [[triiodide]] in solution.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Banin|first1=Uri|last2=Ruhman|first2=Sanford|date=1993-03-15|title=Ultrafast photodissociation of I3. Coherent photochemistry in solution|journal=The Journal of Chemical Physics|volume=98|issue=6|pages=4391–4403|doi=10.1063/1.465066|issn=0021-9606|bibcode=1993JChPh..98.4391B}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Banin|first1=Uri|last2=Waldman|first2=Amir|last3=Ruhman|first3=Sanford|date=1992-02-01|title=Ultrafast photodissociation of I3− in solution: Direct observation of coherent product vibrations|journal=The Journal of Chemical Physics|volume=96|issue=3|pages=2416–2419|doi=10.1063/1.462041|issn=0021-9606|bibcode=1992JChPh..96.2416B|doi-access=free}}</ref>

== Scientific career ==
In 1994 Banin joined the group of [[Paul Alivisatos]] in [[University of California, Berkeley|UC Berkeley]] as a [[postdoctoral researcher]], studying the [[physical chemistry]] of [[semiconductor]] nanocrystals.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Banin|first1=U.|last2=Cerullo|first2=G.|last3=Guzelian|first3=A. A.|last4=Bardeen|first4=C. J.|last5=Alivisatos|first5=A. P.|last6=Shank|first6=C. V.|date=1997-03-15|title=Quantum confinement and ultrafast dephasing dynamics in InP nanocrystals|journal=Physical Review B|volume=55|issue=11|pages=7059–7067|doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.55.7059|bibcode=1997PhRvB..55.7059B}}</ref> In 1997 he joined the Institute of Chemistry at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem as a senior lecturer, becoming a full professor in 2004.<ref name=":3" />

In the early days of his independent career at the Hebrew University, Banin used [[Scanning tunneling spectroscopy|tunneling spectroscopy]] techniques in order to study the electronic properties of semiconductor nanocrystals, ultimately reporting the identification of atomic-like electronic states in 1999 in [[Nature (journal)|Nature]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Banin|first1=Uri|last2=Cao|first2=YunWei|last3=Katz|first3=David|last4=Millo|first4=Oded|date=August 1999|title=Identification of atomic-like electronic states in indium arsenide nanocrystal quantum dots|journal=Nature|volume=400|issue=6744|pages=542–544|doi=10.1038/22979|issn=1476-4687|bibcode=1999Natur.400..542B|s2cid=4424927 }}</ref> His later work has diverged in the directions of both synthesis of novel semiconductor-based nanomaterials, the physical characterization of such nanostructures, as well as various applications. In 2003 his group has reported the first successful growth of [[colloid]]al [[Cubic crystal system|zinc-blende]] lattice [[III-V]] semiconductor nanorods.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Kan|first1=Shihai|last2=Mokari|first2=Taleb|last3=Rothenberg|first3=Eli|last4=Banin|first4=Uri|date=March 2003|title=Synthesis and size-dependent properties of zinc-blende semiconductor quantum rods|journal=Nature Materials|volume=2|issue=3|pages=155–158|doi=10.1038/nmat830|pmid=12612671 |issn=1476-4660|bibcode=2003NatMa...2..155K|s2cid=11711203 }}</ref> Continuing the work on III-V semiconductor nanocrystals, the group has published the synthesis of bright [[near-infrared]]-emitting [[Core–shell semiconductor nanocrystal|core/shell]] nanocrystals,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Cao|last2=Banin|first2=Uri|date=2000-10-01|title=Growth and Properties of Semiconductor Core/Shell Nanocrystals with InAs Cores|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|volume=122|issue=40|pages=9692–9702|doi=10.1021/ja001386g|bibcode=2000JAChS.122.9692C |issn=0002-7863|url=https://figshare.com/articles/Growth_and_Properties_of_Semiconductor_Core_Shell_Nanocrystals_with_InAs_Cores/4008921|url-access=subscription}}</ref> later employing them in a novel nanocrystal-polymer near-infrared [[light-emitting diode]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Tessler|first1=Nir|last2=Medvedev|first2=Vlad|last3=Kazes|first3=Miri|last4=Kan|first4=ShiHai|last5=Banin|first5=Uri|date=2002-02-22|title=Efficient Near-Infrared Polymer Nanocrystal Light-Emitting Diodes|journal=Science|volume=295|issue=5559|pages=1506–1508|doi=10.1126/science.1068153|issn=0036-8075|pmid=11859189|bibcode=2002Sci...295.1506T|s2cid=39611360 }}</ref> In 2011 the group reported a simple procedure for the doping on nanocrystals, allowing the synthesis of heavily-doped p-type and n-type semiconductor nanocrystals.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Mocatta|first1=David|last2=Cohen|first2=Guy|last3=Schattner|first3=Jonathan|last4=Millo|first4=Oded|last5=Rabani|first5=Eran|last6=Banin|first6=Uri|date=2011-04-01|title=Heavily Doped Semiconductor Nanocrystal Quantum Dots|journal=Science|volume=332|issue=6025|pages=77–81|doi=10.1126/science.1196321|issn=0036-8075|pmid=21454783|bibcode=2011Sci...332...77M|arxiv=2105.10877|s2cid=16224129 }}</ref>

Some of his earlier works include the study of [[cadmium]] [[chalcogenide]] molecular clusters as a step between complexes and nanocrystals with semiconducting properties.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Soloviev|first1=V. N.|last2=Eichhöfer|first2=A.|last3=Fenske|first3=D.|last4=Banin|first4=U.|date=2000-03-01|title=Molecular Limit of a Bulk Semiconductor: Size Dependence of the "Band Gap" in CdSe Cluster Molecules|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|volume=122|issue=11|pages=2673–2674|doi=10.1021/ja9940367|bibcode=2000JAChS.122.2673S |issn=0002-7863}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Soloviev|first1=V. N.|last2=Eichhöfer|first2=A.|last3=Fenske|first3=D.|last4=Banin|first4=U.|date=2001-03-01|title=Size-Dependent Optical Spectroscopy of a Homologous Series of CdSe Cluster Molecules|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|volume=123|issue=10|pages=2354–2364|doi=10.1021/ja003598j|pmid=11456885|bibcode=2001JAChS.123.2354S |issn=0002-7863}}</ref> Setting this work aside since 2002, his next paper on the subject was only in 2017 reporting magic sized [[Indium phosphide|InP]] and [[Indium arsenide|InAs]] clusters.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Ning|first1=Jiajia|last2=Banin|first2=Uri|date=2017-02-23|title=Magic size InP and InAs clusters: synthesis, characterization and shell growth|journal=Chemical Communications|language=en|volume=53|issue=17|pages=2626–2629|doi=10.1039/C6CC09778B|pmid=28195285|issn=1364-548X}}</ref> Subsequent work on related clusters with the groups of [[Richard D. Robinson (engineer)|Richard D. Robinson]] and Tobias Hanrath<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Nevers|first1=Douglas R.|last2=Williamson|first2=Curtis B.|last3=Savitzky|first3=Benjamin H.|last4=Hadar|first4=Ido|last5=Banin|first5=Uri|last6=Kourkoutis|first6=Lena F.|last7=Hanrath|first7=Tobias|last8=Robinson|first8=Richard D.|date=2018-03-14|title=Mesophase Formation Stabilizes High-Purity Magic-Sized Clusters|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|volume=140|issue=10|pages=3652–3662|doi=10.1021/jacs.7b12175|pmid=29376343|issn=0002-7863|arxiv=1906.10997|bibcode=2018JAChS.140.3652N |s2cid=3838360 }}</ref> has finally lead to the discovery of the reversible [[isomerization]] of inorganic clusters<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Williamson|first1=Curtis B.|last2=Nevers|first2=Douglas R.|last3=Nelson|first3=Andrew|last4=Hadar|first4=Ido|last5=Banin|first5=Uri|last6=Hanrath|first6=Tobias|last7=Robinson|first7=Richard D.|date=2019-02-15|title=Chemically reversible isomerization of inorganic clusters|journal=Science|language=en|volume=363|issue=6428|pages=731–735|doi=10.1126/science.aau9464|issn=0036-8075|pmid=30765565|bibcode=2019Sci...363..731W|arxiv=1906.10984|s2cid=62860050 }}</ref> – a discovery made by chance during the shipping of the samples. This work was called "the final bridge" between molecules and nanocrystals.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.chemistryworld.com/inorganic-isomerism-uncovered-in-cadmium-sulfide-clusters/3010123.article|title=Inorganic isomerism uncovered in cadmium sulfide clusters|last=Andy Extance2019-02-14T19:00:00+00:00|website=Chemistry World|language=en|access-date=2019-11-16}}</ref>

One of the most recognized contribution of Banin to the field of colloidal nanostructures is the first demonstration of selective metal growth on semiconductor nanocrystals,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Mokari|first1=Taleb|last2=Rothenberg|first2=Eli|last3=Popov|first3=Inna|last4=Costi|first4=Ronny|last5=Banin|first5=Uri|date=2004-06-18|title=Selective Growth of Metal Tips onto Semiconductor Quantum Rods and Tetrapods|journal=Science|volume=304|issue=5678|pages=1787–1790|doi=10.1126/science.1097830|issn=0036-8075|pmid=15205530|bibcode=2004Sci...304.1787M|s2cid=36848680 }}</ref> resembling well-known bulk systems such as the [[Schottky diode]], and the subsequent refinement of related synthesis procedures and the discovery of similar structures,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Mokari|first1=Taleb|last2=Sztrum|first2=Claudia G.|last3=Salant|first3=Asaf|last4=Rabani|first4=Eran|last5=Banin|first5=Uri|date=November 2005|title=Formation of asymmetric one-sided metal-tipped semiconductor nanocrystal dots and rods|journal=Nature Materials|volume=4|issue=11|pages=855–863|doi=10.1038/nmat1505|issn=1476-4660|bibcode=2005NatMa...4..855M|s2cid=137604997 }}</ref> as well as the physical characterization of such systems.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Costi|first1=Ronny|last2=Cohen|first2=Guy|last3=Salant|first3=Asaf|last4=Rabani|first4=Eran|last5=Banin|first5=Uri|date=2009-05-13|title=Electrostatic Force Microscopy Study of Single Au−CdSe Hybrid Nanodumbbells: Evidence for Light-Induced Charge Separation|journal=Nano Letters|volume=9|issue=5|pages=2031–2039|doi=10.1021/nl900301v|pmid=19435381|issn=1530-6984|bibcode=2009NanoL...9.2031C}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Steiner|first1=D.|last2=Mokari|first2=T.|last3=Banin|first3=U.|last4=Millo|first4=O.|date=2005-07-28|title=Electronic Structure of Metal-Semiconductor Nanojunctions in Gold CdSe Nanodumbbells|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=95|issue=5|article-number=056805|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.95.056805|pmid=16090904|bibcode=2005PhRvL..95e6805S}}</ref> To this day, hybrid metal-semiconductor nanostructures are [[State of the art|state-of-the-art]] systems in the field of [[photocatalysis]]. One of the breakthroughs made by Banin's lab, employing hybrid metal-semiconductor nanocrystals in water-based [[3D printing]] and [[photopolymerization]] of common [[acrylate]]s.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Pawar|first1=Amol Ashok|last2=Halivni|first2=Shira|last3=Waiskopf|first3=Nir|last4=Ben-Shahar|first4=Yuval|last5=Soreni-Harari|first5=Michal|last6=Bergbreiter|first6=Sarah|last7=Banin|first7=Uri|last8=Magdassi|first8=Shlomo|date=2017-07-12|title=Rapid Three-Dimensional Printing in Water Using Semiconductor–Metal Hybrid Nanoparticles as Photoinitiators|journal=Nano Letters|volume=17|issue=7|pages=4497–4501|doi=10.1021/acs.nanolett.7b01870|pmid=28617606|issn=1530-6984|bibcode=2017NanoL..17.4497P|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://phys.org/news/2017-08-rapid-d-hybrid-nanoparticles.html|title=Rapid 3-D printing in water using novel hybrid nanoparticles|website=phys.org|access-date=2019-11-15}}</ref> It was also later shown that such approach can also be used for [[Bulk polymerization|solvent-free]] photopolymerization and [[microprinting]].<ref>{{Cite journal
|last1=Verbitsky |first1=Lior|last2=Waiskopf |first2=Nir|last3=Magdassi |first3=Shlomo |author-link3=Shlomo Magdassi|last4=Banin |first4=Uri|date=2019-06-13|title=A clear solution: semiconductor nanocrystals as photoinitiators in solvent free polymerization
|journal=Nanoscale|volume=11|issue=23|pages=11209–11216|doi=10.1039/C9NR03086G|pmid=31157812|s2cid=173995422|issn=2040-3372
}}</ref>

Banin is widely recognized as a pioneer of nanoscience in Israel, founding the [[Harvey M. Kreuger Family Center for Nanoscience and Nanotechnology]] in 2001 and serving as its first director for nearly a decade until 2010.<ref name=":1" /> He was the chairman of the scientific committee and a co-chairperson of the first international nanoscience conference in Israel in 2009,<ref name=":3" /> now an internationally-recognized biennial conference.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.kenesexhibitions.com/nanoisrael/previous-events/|title=Previous Events|website=Nano Israel 2019 Conference and Exhibition|access-date=2019-11-15}}</ref>

In 2009, Banin became the scientific founder of Qlight Nanotech, which was later fully acquired by [[Merck Group|Merck KGaA]] for an undisclosed price and is currently located in the campus of the Hebrew University in [[Givat Ram]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://new.huji.ac.il/en/article/27100|title=Merck to Fully Acquire Qlight Nanotech, a Spinoff Company of Hebrew University's Yissum {{!}} האוניברסיטה העברית בירושלים {{!}} The Hebrew University of Jerusalem|website=new.huji.ac.il|access-date=2019-11-15}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.timesofisrael.com/merck-ceo-sees-firms-future-intertwined-with-israels/|title=Merck CEO sees firm's future intertwined with Israel's|last=Shamah|first=David|website=[[The Times of Israel]]|date=30 June 2015 |language=en-US|access-date=2019-11-19 |issn=0040-7909}}</ref> In 2019 [[Nanosys]] signed an exclusive agreement on quantum dot patents developed in Banin's lab and held by [[Yissum Research Development Company of the Hebrew University|Yissum]].<ref>{{Cite press release|url=https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/nanosys-signs-exclusive-license-agreement-for-control-of-yissum-quantum-dot-patent-portfolio-300902832.html|title=Nanosys Signs Exclusive License Agreement for Control of Yissum Quantum Dot Patent Portfolio|last=Nanosys|website=www.prnewswire.com|access-date=2019-11-15}}</ref>

Banin has been an associate editor of the [[American Chemical Society]] journal [[Nano Letters]] between 2013-2021.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=https://pubs.acs.org/page/nalefd/editors.html|title=Editorial Board|website=pubs.acs.org|access-date=2019-11-15}}</ref> In 2020 he joined the [[Advisory board|Advisory Board]] of [[Nanoscale Horizons]], a journal published by the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]].<ref>{{Cite journal|date=2020|title=Introducing the new Nanoscale Horizons Advisory Board members|url=http://xlink.rsc.org/?DOI=D0NH90036B|journal=Nanoscale Horizons|language=en|volume=5|issue=8|page=1146|doi=10.1039/D0NH90036B|pmid=32647848 |bibcode=2020NanoH...5.1146. |s2cid=220473267 |issn=2055-6756|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

As of 2022, Banin has authored more than 210 papers that have been widely cited.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Uri Banin - Google Scholar Citations|url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?hl=en&user=1GtEMWgAAAAJ|access-date=2020-09-27|website=scholar.google.com}}</ref> In addition, he has invented more than 35 different patents.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://patents.google.com/?inventor=Uri+Banin|title=Google Patents|website=patents.google.com|access-date=2019-12-13}}</ref>
